exail_rescreen.finding: Exail was excluded on the test "is it an aerial UAV OEM". That is not the landscape test: the UAV Ecosystem branch already admits Navigation / GNSS and Components suppliers who build no aircraft, including SBG Systems (France, inertial navigation, included) and Civitanavi (Italy, whose own record reads "an ecosystem supplier, not a UAV OEM", included).
corrections_to_the_earlier_package: WRONG: "the newest IT180 material on exail.com is a 2015 ECA press release". An Exail newsroom item of 1 July 2023 calls the IT180-60 "its" aerial drone and quotes the Director of the Land and Air robotics division at Exail.

WRONG: "UMIS integrates third-party UAVs rather than establishing Exail as an aerial UAV OEM". The Exail-branded UMIS datasheet (2022-07-29) lists Unmanned Aerial Vehicles among the toolbox vehicles and says Exail provides unmanned systems "at sea and in the air". Third-party integration is an additional open-architecture capability, not the basis of the UAV listing.
HALF RIGHT: "the current robotics page lists no aerial family". No aerial platform page, but the Defense range carries a "Land and air navigation & pointing" category.
RIGHT: the 12 UAV-categorised products are all maritime, and Exail has zero company_sectors rows.
primary_aerial_evidence: Airbus SIRTAP tactical UAS, 12 May 2025: Exail UmiX-40 IMU supplied for the navigation system of a named unmanned aerial system. This is exactly the "Exail-owned aerial evidence" the exclusion note was waiting for.
AIR & LAND DEFENSE ROBOTIC SOLUTIONS brochure, Exail-branded, 2023-01-29: UAVs listed as an Exail solution line; C2 system controls multiple UGVs and UAVs.
UMIS datasheet, Exail-branded, 2022-07-29: unmanned systems "at sea and in the air"; UAV among the toolbox vehicles.
Neptis, 9 October 2026: Counter-Uncrewed Aerial Systems (C-UAS) listed among mission areas. Secondary.
